rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning applies only after the person hears the ruling, distinguishing someone who alters a will without hearing from someone who alters it after hearing.
rows.anchor: يسمع، أو بدل وقد سمع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An executor must carry out a will without waiting for a judge; carrying it out without alteration fulfills the duty.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب على الوصي تنفيذ الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ownership by heirs and legatees is a legal ruling bestowed by God, not a transfer from the deceased; a legator's condition may still be honored after his ownership ends when beneficial.
rows.anchor: هي أحكام شرعية تملك الورثة من جهة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers geminate موص; others read it lightly. Both forms are synonyms for وصى and أوصى.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب: موص بالتشديد،

rows.speaker: علي (عليه السلام)
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ali has حيفا instead of جنفا, which the author takes as an explanation of جنف.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي (عليه السلام) حيفا بالحاء والياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنف means deviation in speech and affairs, rooted in departing from what is straight.
rows.anchor: الجنف: الميل في الكلام والأمور كلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun بينهم refers either to the legatees and their disputants, inferred from context, or to parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: الضمير في قوله: (بينهم) يرجع على معلوم بالدلالة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فلا إثم عليه can refer to the testator or the reconciler, implicit in the meaning.
rows.anchor: والضمير في قوله: (فلا إثم عليه) يرجع على الموصي،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands the fear to arise while the testator consults about the will and signs of deviation appear, prompting correction.
rows.anchor: أي إذا خاف وهو يشاوره في الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that after making a will that deviates, the testator fears the deviation will persist, revokes it, and writes a rightful will.
rows.anchor: إذا أوصى ومال عن الحق، وخاف أن يستمر أصلحه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada place correction after the testator dies: fear of deviation in execution leads to a compromise between heirs and beneficiaries.
rows.anchor: إذا أوصى واستقرت الوصية، ومات الموصي، وخاف العدول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also glossed as feared, knew, or was aware; the موص is the deceased who made the will.
rows.anchor: فمن خاف وقيل: خشي، وقيل: علم من موص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid distinguish accidental or interpretive deviation from right, called جنف, from deliberate wrongdoing, called sin.
rows.anchor: قيل: جنفا: ميلا عن الحق على جهة الخطأ والتأويل أو إثما تعمدا لذلك، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد.

rows.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
rows.claim: Ata and Qatada give جنف the general sense of deviation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ميلا، عن عطاء وقتادة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the wrongdoing as making a bequest above one third of the estate.
rows.anchor: قيل: إذا زاد على الثلث، عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies it as diverting a bequest from its proper place by bequeathing to someone outside the kin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أن يعدل عن موضع الوصية، فيوصي لغير قرابته، عن الحسن.

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus gives the example of bequeathing to a son's child to keep the estate from going to one's son.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أن يوصي لابن ابنه، كيلا يكون المال لابنه، عن طاووس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the broad account that the terms mean deviation from the legally prescribed course.
rows.anchor: عن الطريق المشروع، وهو الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reconciler may be the executor, authorities, a mediator, or a witness among the parties.
rows.anchor: قيل: المصلح هو الوصي، وقيل: الولاة، وقيل: المتوسط،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reconciliation may be among will beneficiaries or between beneficiaries and heirs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بين أهل الوصايا، وقيل: بين أهل الوصية، وأهل الميراث،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reconciliation restores the matter to its rightful state through correction and mediation.
rows.anchor: والإصلاح أن يرد الأمر إلى حقه بالإصلاح والتوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sin means no blame, and the assurance may apply to the executor or mediator.
rows.anchor: قيل: على الوصي، وقيل: على المتوسط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that God judges His servants, disproving determinism: if all acts were created by God, judgment of people would be meaningless.
rows.anchor: كانت مخلوقة لله تعالى لم يكن للحساب مع العباد معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward and punishment are deserved for acts of the heart as well as other acts.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الثواب والعقاب يستحق في أفعال القلوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills; this passage does not specify who, a point clarified elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه يغفر لمن يشاء، ويعذب من يشاء،

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read singular كتابه, meaning either the Quran or a collective singular; the author prefers the plural for agreement with surrounding plurals and the majority reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي. وكتابه على الواحد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan stills the sin in رسله to ease successive vowels; Ibn Umar and Nafi also transmit shortened كتبه and رسله, while others lengthen them.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن بتسكينه لكثرة الحركات،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ويعقوب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Yaqub read لا يفرق in the third person, referring to the Messenger or all messengers; others read in the first-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير ويعقوب لا يفرق بالياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common first-person plural reading fits the following وقالوا: the believers say that they do not distinguish among messengers.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالنون على معنى، وقالوا: لا نفرق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically iman means assent, which is the sense here; religiously it names all obligations. It can occur without praise, as belief in Musaylima, while unqualified usage praises.
rows.anchor: الإيمان: التصديق في اللغة، وهو المراد بالآية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب is the plural of كتاب.
rows.anchor: وكتب: جمع كتاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المصير means return.
rows.anchor: والمصير: المرجع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's clause has its own subject and predicate; المؤمنون likewise begins a separate clause with كل آمن as its predicate.
rows.anchor: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه ابتداء وخبره على حدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted objects are His saying and His command: they heard what God said and obeyed His command, as praise of them indicates.
rows.anchor: والمحذوف من قوله: سمعنا وأطعنا يعني سمعنا قوله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غفرانك is accusative as a verbal noun in place of a request such as forgive us; al-Farra also allows nominative, construing it as a declaration of worship.
rows.anchor: ونصب غفرانك لأنه بدل من الفعل المأخوذ منه،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows غفرانك to be nominative, with an implied meaning that God's forgiveness is their worship.
rows.anchor: ويجوز رفع غفرانك على تقدير: غفرانك تعبدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربنا is accusative as a vocative in the sense O our Lord.
rows.anchor: (ربنا) نصب على يا ربنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase omits its complement: the return is to God's reward or judgment, as in Ibrahim's saying he is going to his Lord, meaning His command.
rows.anchor: وإليك المصير) فيه محذوف. قيل: وإلى جزائك أو إلى حكمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the believers' wording with the criminals' statement ربنا أبصرنا in 32:12.
rows.anchor: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim transmits from Ata that the polytheists asked Muhammad for a sign, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: حكى شيخنا أبو القاسم عن عطاء أن المشركين قالوا: أرنا يا محمد آية،

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata's report through Ibn Jarir says that after the Prophet came to Medina and the one-God verse was revealed, Quraysh in Mecca asked how one God could suffice people, and this verse followed.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن جرير عن عطاء أنه لما قدم النبي

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى
rows.claim: Abu al-Duha reports that polytheists reacted to the one-God verse by demanding a sign if Muhammad were truthful, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي الضحى: لما نزل قوله: وإلهكم إله واحد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن مسروق
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Masruq reports that Quraysh asked Jews and Christians about Moses' and Jesus' signs, then asked Muhammad to turn Safa to gold; God offered to grant it with severe punishment for disbelief, but Muhammad asked time to invite them, and the verse came to show creation is a greater proof.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن مسروق قال: سألت قريش اليهود فقالوا: حدثونا عما جاءكم به موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing oneness, God adduces proofs that cannot rightly be ignored, removes the excuse of reflective people, and directs them to know Him through His acts and signs instead of imitation.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى ما تقدم من التوحيد عقبه بذكر الأدلة مبينا أنه لا يجوز العدول عنها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth means bringing them into being by measured origination.
rows.anchor: يعني في إنشائها مقدرا على سبيل الاختراع

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ata and Ibn Kaysan explain the variation as differences in kind, color, length, and shortness; another explanation is that night and day succeed one another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اختلافهما في الجنس واللون والطول والقصر، عن عطاء وابن كيسان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is named before day because it is the original state and light is incidental: God created the earth dark before sun and moon.
rows.anchor: لأن الليل هو الأصل، والضياء طارئ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are gathered where judgment is made, and no one besides God has authority there.
rows.anchor: تجمعون إلى الموضع الذي يحكم فيه بينكم، لا حكم لأحد هناك غيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to remember God is best understood as takbirs during the Tashriq days, which are specific to those days.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يحمل على تكبير أيام التشريق؛ لأنه المختص بهذه الأيام،

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Umar, Ali, and Ibn Masud agree that takbir begins at Fajr on Arafah.
rows.anchor: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود، واتفقوا أنه من صلاة الفجر يوم عرفة،

rows.speaker: علي (عليه السلام)
rows.claim: Ali ends takbir at Asr on the final Tashriq day; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad follow this view, which the author says is Muslim practice in the cities and Abu Ali's choice.
rows.anchor: فقال علي (عليه السلام): إلى العصر من آخر أيام التشريق،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Ibn Masud ends the takbir at Asr on the day of sacrifice; Abu Hanifa follows this view.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: إلى صلاة العصر من يوم النحر، وهو قول أبي حنيفة.

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: One report from Umar ends takbir at Dhuhr on the final Tashriq day; another report matches Ali's later ending.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر إلى صلاة الظهر من آخر أيام التشريق.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Zayd agree that takbir begins at Dhuhr on Sacrifice day.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد، اتفقوا أنها من صلاة الظهر يوم النحر،

rows.speaker: زيد وعطاء
rows.claim: Zayd ends takbir at Asr on the final Tashriq day; Ata agrees, and this is also reported from Abu Yusuf.
rows.anchor: فقال زيد: إلى العصر من آخر أيام التشريق، وهو قول عطاء،

rows.speaker: ابن عمر والشافعي
rows.claim: Ibn Umar's view, adopted by al-Shafii, ends the takbir at Fajr on the final Tashriq day.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: إلى صلاة الفجر من آخر أيام التشريق، وهو قول الشافعي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas ends takbir at Dhuhr on the final Tashriq day.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إلى صلاة الظهر من آخر أيام التشريق.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Abu Hanifa, and his companions say the takbir is pronounced twice.
rows.anchor: فيقول: الله أكبر مرتين، عن ابن مسعود وأبي حنيفة وأصحابه،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والشافعي
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Shafii say takbir is pronounced three times.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ثلاث مرات، وهو قول الشافعي،

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas says Allahu akbar, pauses, then says Allahu akbar followed by la ilaha illa Allah.
rows.anchor: وكان مالك بن أنس يقول: الله أكبر، ثم يقطع، ثم يقول: الله أكبر،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada gives a longer formula: Allahu akbar kabira, Allahu akbar for guiding us, and praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: الله أكبر كبيرا، الله أكبر على ما هدانا،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires takbir from accountable, free, resident men praying an obligatory prayer in a recommended congregation in a central town.
rows.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة يجب بخمس شرائط على الرجال المكلفين الأحرار المقيمين

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say everyone who performs an obligatory prayer must say takbir.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: كل من صلى فرضا كبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hastening or delaying refers to stoning the pillars, the rite specific to these days; either schedule is permitted without blame.
rows.anchor: وما ذلك إلا رمي الجمار؛ لأنها تختص بهذه الأيام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Sacrifice day throw seven pebbles at Aqaba, stop talbiya at the first, say takbir with every pebble, and stone no other pillar.
rows.anchor: يوم النحر يرمي جمرة العقبة بسبع حصيات يقطع التلبية عند أول حصاة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the next day, the first Tashriq day, stone all three pillars after noon in sequence; pause by the first two but not Aqaba.
rows.anchor: وفي اليوم الثاني وهو أول أيام التشريق يرمي الجمار الثلاث بعد الزوال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives three possibilities for Jews denying the Day of Judgment: some alone said it; it was a debating ploy; or they abandoned their predecessors' view to avoid its shame, as in saying Ezra is God's son.
rows.anchor: قلنا: يحتمل أنه كان قول بعضهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns the Jews' severe hostility to Gabriel and declares them unbelievers deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: وتدل على عظم عداوة جبريل؛ لذلك ذمهم، وألزمهم الكفر والعذاب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce Mikal with a kasra and no hamza, on the pattern mifal.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب وحفص عن عاصم ميكال بكسر الميم،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
rows.claim: Abu Jafar and Nafi read ميكائل with hamza and no following ya.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: وميكائل مختلسين

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers lengthen the form and pronounce the hamza, reading ميكائيل.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالمد والهمز

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Another valid form is shortened hamzated ميكئل, transmitted from al-Amash; the author prefers Mikal as the Hijazi form.
rows.anchor: وفيه لغة أخرى ميكئل مقصور مهموز على وزن ميكعل،

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed line about Badr pairs Gabriel and Mikal as supporting forces, illustrating Mikal.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: ويوم بدر لقيناكم لنا مدد

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's verse attests the form ميكالا alongside جبرئيل.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير: عبدوا الصليب وكذبوا بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though malak's root is associated with a message, it became specific to a kind of creature, so it is coordinated with messengers.
rows.anchor: الملك وإن كان أصله من الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسل is the plural of رسول.
rows.anchor: والرسل جمع رسول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw before Gabriel and Michael may coordinate them or mean or, so hostility to either entails hostility to all.
rows.anchor: قلنا: فيه قولان: الأول: أنه واو العطف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enmity to God cannot literally mean seeking to harm Him, which is impossible; it means acting as an enemy through opposition and disobedience.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح العداوة مع الله؛ لأنه طلب الإضرار به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes enmity to God as hostility directed against Him, like the wording about those who harm God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد معاداة، كقوله: (إن الذين يؤذون الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel and Michael are named separately despite being angels to exalt them; another explanation says this removes ambiguity and emphasizes the subject of dispute.
rows.anchor: وإنما أعاد ذكرهما وإن دخلا في جملة الملائكة تفضيلا لهما وتفخيما لشأنهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enmity means inflicting harm and lasting punishment; disbelief in any one of those named is disbelief in all and brings recompense.
rows.anchor: فإن الله عدو للكافرين يعني يفعل بهم فعل المعادي من الإضرار والعقاب الدائم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min appears before the polytheists because they are a subset of people; comparative construction works this way when the compared group is included in the larger class.
rows.anchor: لأنهم بعض الناس، والإضافة في باب أفعل لا تكون إلا كذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without min, one cannot call a ruby better than glass as a member of that class; it can be called best among stones because it is one of them.
rows.anchor: الياقوت أفضل من الزجاج، ولا يجوز الياقوت أفضل الزجاج؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews are not Magians but are among humanity, explaining min in the comparison.
rows.anchor: فلذلك قال: ومن الذين أشركوا؛ لأن اليهود ليسوا من المجوس،

rows.speaker: أبو علي والقاضي
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that Jews are God's beloved and most entitled to truth: their insistence on earthly life despite its griefs shows stubbornness, not sincere certainty of Paradise.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على بطلان قولهم: نحن أحباء الله، وإنا أحق بالحق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long life without obedience to God brings no benefit and becomes regret; length of life matters when joined with good works.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن طول العمر إذا لم يكن في طاعة الله لا يغني شيئا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking long life for worldly aims is blameworthy; seeking time for obedience and making up missed good works is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الحرص على طول البقاء لطلب الدنيا ونحوها مذموم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealment is hiding something when it needs to be made known, the opposite of disclosure.
rows.anchor: الكتمان: إخفاء الشيء مع الحاجة إلى إظهاره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyinat are proofs and signs; bayyina is the singular.
rows.anchor: والبينات: الحجج والعلامات، واحدها بينة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'n means expulsion and distance.
rows.anchor: واللعن: الطرد والإبعاد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ansar asked Jews about the Prophet's description and rulings in the Torah, which they concealed, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن جماعة من الأنصار سألوا نفرا من اليهود

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي
rows.claim: Hasan and Abu Ali say the verse was revealed about the People of the Book as a warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أهل الكتاب، عن الحسن وأبي علي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the true religion, God urges disclosure and forbids concealment.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى دين الحق حث على إظهاره ونهى عن كتمانه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والحسن والربيع والسدي والأصم وأبو علي
rows.claim: One view identifies those concealing revelation as Jews and Christians among the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قيل: أهل الكتاب من اليهود والنصارى، عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another view treats this as a general statement about anyone who conceals God's revelation; al-Qadi says the occasion does not restrict it, and reports from Aisha and Abu Hurayra support generality.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كلام مستأنف في كل من كتم ما أنزل الله، عن أبي القاسم وأبي مسلم.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says that but for two verses from God's book he would not have narrated, then recites the warning about concealing revelation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: لولا آيتان من كتاب الله تعالى ما حدثتكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes clear proofs arguments revealed in books and guidance rational evidence, distinguishing religious sciences from proofs of reason.
rows.anchor: قيل: من الحجج المنزلة في الكتب، والهدى: الدلائل،

words: مِن بَعْدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي الْكِتَابِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clarification in the book may refer to the Prophet's description and rulings in Torah and Gospel, a revealed book generally, or earlier scriptures first and the Quran second.
rows.anchor: قيل: في التوراة والإنجيل من صفته

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع وأبو علي
rows.claim: One view identifies the cursers as angels and believers.
rows.anchor: قيل: الملائكة والمؤمنون، عن قتادة والربيع وأبي علي.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say the cursers are earth's animals and vermin, which say rain is withheld because of human sin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دواب الأرض وهوامها يقولون: منعنا القطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals receive a rational-person expression because an action of rational beings is attributed to them, like the expression about seeing them prostrating.
rows.anchor: ولذا عبر عنهم بعبارة ما يعقل؛ لأنه أضيف إليهم فعل ما يعقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the cursers are everything except humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: قيل: كل شيء سوى الثقلين الجن والإنس، عن ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Muslim identify the cursers as those who believe in the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من آمن به، عن الأصم وأبي مسلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may be general and include the people of Hell, who curse those who concealed religion from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن أهل النار تلعنهم أيضا حيث كتموهم الدين،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says when two people curse one another, the curse falls on the deserving one; if neither deserves it, it returns to the Jews who concealed revelation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: إذا تلاعن المتلاعنان وقعت اللعنة على المستحق،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says concealers receive two curses, from God and all creatures; in the grave the dead person is struck and cries out, and all who hear except humans and jinn curse him.
rows.anchor: لعنتين: لعنة الله، ولعنة الخلائق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Confirming Talut's kingship by this sign helps the Israelites submit; kingship needs no miracle, but if confirmed by one it is a miracle for the prophet, since miracles cannot appear through a non-prophet.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على تأكيد ملك طالوت بهذه الآية؛ ليكونوا أقرب إلى الانقياد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark contains something that reassures the Israelites, so its return is a divine favor.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن في التابوت ما يسكنون إليه، لذلك من عليهم برده عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage demonstrates the greatness of God's favors to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وتدل على عظيم نعم الله تعالى على بني إسرائيل.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers pronounce غرفة with fatha, others with damma: the first marks an act of scooping and the second the amount in hand; both are sound.
rows.anchor: قرأ غرفة بفتح الغين ابن كثير وأبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The common reading has قليلا in the accusative, while Ibn Masud is reported with the nominative.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة قليلا بالنصب، وعن ابن مسعود بالرفع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has nahr with an open ha; some read it with a still ha, and both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة نهر بفتح الهاء، وعن بعضهم بالجزم، وكلاهما لغتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasl means cutting; to depart from a place is described as cutting away and passing beyond it.
rows.anchor: الفصل: مصدر فصلت الشيء فصلا، والفصل أصله القطع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jund is a plural for a large body and ajnad for a small one; its root is thick ground, a place of support against hardship.
rows.anchor: والجنود: جمع جند للكثير، والأجناد للقليل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharf is scooping water by hand; ghurfa with fatha is the instance of scooping and with damma its resulting amount.
rows.anchor: والغرف مصدر غرفت الماء بيدي، وبالغرفة غرفا بالفتح،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtala, imtahana, and ikhtabara are synonyms.
rows.anchor: والابتلاء والامتحان والاختبار نظائر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr is a watercourse; its plurals are nahr and anhar and its root denotes breadth; the word has open and still ha pronunciations.
rows.anchor: والنهر: مجرى الماء وجمعه نهر وأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujawaza is passing beyond something without obstruction; jawz is its middle, and passing over a sin is to overlook it.
rows.anchor: والمجاوزة: من الجواز وهو المرور من غير شيء يصد

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: One interpretation is to remember God through studying, teaching, and learning scripture and Sunnah; God remembers worshippers with praise, and the verse commands knowing God, His Messenger, and His laws.
rows.anchor: بالمدح والثناء، فيكون أمرا بذكر الله والدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving thanks for God's blessing means obeying Him and not denying His favor through disobedience.
rows.anchor: واشكروا لي أي اشكروا نعمتي بالطاعة ولا تكفرون بالعصيان.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God remembers an obedient person with good, while He remembers a disobedient person with a curse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: من ذكر الله تعالى من أهل طاعته ذكره الله بخير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates and provides before people remember Him; the conditional remembrance here means honoring and praising them, which depends on their remembrance.
rows.anchor: المراد ذكره إيانا على وجه التعظيم والمدح وذلك يتعلق بالشرط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All worship counts as remembrance: seeking knowledge, resolving doubts, intending obedience, repenting, affirming God's lordship, praising Him, praying, fasting, and other rites.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن جميع العبادات تدخل في الذكر لذلك أوجب ذكره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembering people means reward, mercy, and recompense.
rows.anchor: فأما ذكره إيانا فالمراد الثواب والرحمة والجزاء.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains shiq as a crack, rooted in cutting something and making it have sides.
rows.anchor: والشق: الصدع، قال الزجاج: وأصله قطع الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafla is heedlessness, the mind's loss of awareness; taghaful is deliberately acting as if unaware.
rows.anchor: والغفلة: السهو عن الشيء، وهو ذهاب المعنى عن النفس،

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says aw can mean rather, as in the verse saying one hundred thousand or more.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه بل أشد قسوة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts make aw express doubt, ambiguity, permission, or and; the author prefers permission: compare them to stones or something harder, as in sit with Hasan or Ibn Sirin.
rows.anchor: والاختيار الإباحة؛ لأنه مشهور عندهم ظاهر في مفهوم الآية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis coordinates أشد قسوة with the syntactic position of kāf.
rows.anchor: بم ارتفع أو أشد؟ قلنا: فيه وجهان: أحدهما: أن يكون عطفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second grammatical analysis attaches it to an implied هي.
rows.anchor: والثاني: على أو هي أشد قسوة.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that their hearts became hard and dry.
rows.anchor: قيل: اشتدت ويبست، عن الكلبي،

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their hearts lost tenderness, mercy, and humility; other glosses say they thickened or blackened.
rows.anchor: وقيل: غلظت، وقيل: اسودت، وقيل: ذهب منها اللين والرحمة والخشوع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view addresses those who denied killing the victim even after he was revived and identified the killers.
rows.anchor: بعد أن حيي وذكر أنهم قتلوه ومات أنكروا

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm addresses Jewish rabbis whose worldly desire and pride made them reject truth and resist admonition.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خطاب لأحبار اليهود؛ لأنهم لأجل طلب الدنيا والاستكبار لا يقبلون الحق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views address all Jews or Jews living in the Prophet's time; Abu Muslim reports the latter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خطاب لجميع اليهود، وقيل: خطاب لمن كان في عصر النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is after the resurrection of the dead; al-Asamm says after the earlier signs, including resurrection, transformation, and raising the mountain.
rows.anchor: قيل: من بعد إحياء الميت، وقيل: بعد تلك الآيات المتقدمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the victim revived when struck with part of the cow, named his nephews as killers, then died; they denied killing him and swore they had not.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما ضرب المقتول ببعض البقرة جلس حيا، وقال: قتلني بنو أخي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts resemble stones because they do not soften at admonition or a sign.
rows.anchor: شبه قلوبهم بالحجارة لصلابتها، يعني لا تلين لموعظة وآية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One comparison says stones respond to God's will while their hearts flee from it.
rows.anchor: قيل: لأن الحجارة تتصرف على مراد الله تعالى، وقلوبهم تنفر من ذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another comparison is that people's evil deeds do not appear in stones, while stones have benefits that their hearts lack.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد ما يظهر منهم من الأفعال القبيحة، ولا يظهر من الحجر،

words: وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones split open and rivers flow from them; one view identifies Moses' stone that released twelve springs, while another takes the statement generally.
rows.anchor: يعني يتشقق عن الماء، فيسيل منه الأنهار، وقيل: المراد به الحجر الذي كان مع موسى

words: وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in منه refers to ما; another report links منها to the stones.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منه يرجع إلى (ما)، وروي عن بعضهم منها يرجع إلى الأحجار

words: وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes take منها as referring to stones; Abu Muslim instead says it means hearts that humble in fear, among them believing People of the Book.
rows.anchor: يرجع إلى الحجارة، يعني: وفي الحجارة ما يهبط من خشية الله،

words: وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads منها as hearts that humble in fear of God, namely believers among the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يرجع على القلوب، وتقديره: من القلوب ما يهبط من خشية الله تعالى،

words: وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those referring the pronoun to stones, one explanation is that hail descends from fear of God, compared with God's appointed guardians over people.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو البرد يهبط لخشية الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the Shiite argument that anyone who ever sinned is unfit for imamate, used to attack Abu Bakr and Umar: the verse concerns prophethood.
rows.anchor: ظلم مرة، وراموا بذلك الطعن على أبي بكر وعمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A repentant wrongdoer is no longer described as a wrongdoer in that condition; the covenant is withheld from a person who remains in that state.
rows.anchor: وبعد، فإن الظالم متى تاب لا يوصف بأنه ظالم به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham knew prophethood was unsuitable for a wrongdoer but did not know his descendants' status; God clarified that some would be wrongdoers and prophecy goes to those who are not.
rows.anchor: قلنا: بلى، ولكن لم يعلم حال ذريته، فبين تعالى أن فيهم من هذا حاله،

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read واتخذوا with open kha as a report, coordinated with جعلنا; others read it with kasra as a command.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر: واتخذوا بفتح الخاء على الخبر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consensus reading is singular مثابة; some transmit the plural مثابات.
rows.anchor: والقراءة المجمع عليها مثابة على الواحد،

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hafs from Asim opens the ya in بيتي according to the original; other readers still it for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم: بيتي بفتح الياء على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayt can mean refuge, home, or dwelling; Bayt Allah is the Kaaba, and the word also means a poetic line or a human or tribal house.
rows.anchor: البيت والمأوى والمنزل نظائر، وبيت الله هو الكعبة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayt can also refer to entering at night, doing something at night as opposed to during the day, or raiding people at night.
rows.anchor: والبيتوتة: دخولك في الليل، وبت أفعل كذا، كما تقول في النهار: ظللت،

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Mathaba comes from returning; Fara and Zajjaj say مثابة and مثاب have the same sense, like maqama and maqam.
rows.anchor: والمثابة: من ثاب يثوب مثابة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats مثابة as an intensive form, like نسابة or علامة.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في مثابة مبالغة كما في قولهم: نسابة وعلامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musalla is a place of prayer.
rows.anchor: والمصلى: موضع الصلاة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taif is one who circles; tawaf means going around something.
rows.anchor: والطائف: الدائر، طاف يطوف طوفا وطوافا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akafa means to remain attached to something or stay with it; some say turn toward it without turning away. Mu'takif and akif name a mosque resident, and akafa would also be correct for i'takafa.
rows.anchor: والعكف: مصدر عكف يعكف بضم الكاف وكسرها عكفا،
